title: Align toolchain version constraints
why: A checked-in toolchain pin outside the root manifest's supported range makes local or CI verification disagree with the declared project contract.
suggestion: Update the toolchain pin or the manifest requirement so the checked-in development and CI environments satisfy the declared range.
limitations: Root Node.js engines are compared with .nvmrc, .node-version, and literal CI node-version pins; root requires-python is compared with .python-version and literal CI python-version pins, while CI workflows that explicitly reference a compatible nested Python project use that project's constraint.

Root Cargo rust-version is compared with rust-toolchain.toml and literal numeric CI toolchain pins; root Maven compiler release, source, or java.version is compared with .java-version and literal CI java-version pins.

Simple exact, comparison, caret, and tilde conjunctions are evaluated; partial pins such as Node.js 20 are treated as floating channels and abstain when a more precise requirement overlaps them. Disjunctions, dynamic matrices, named channels such as stable, prereleases, Gradle toolchains, and organization-level CI are excluded.
